text:
mara: Quick check — we're planning a contract change to include an optional `metadata` object on text generation responses (reason: observability + prompt provenance). Proposal: dual-shipping for 6 weeks where both shapes are returned and clients can opt-in via an `Accept-Response-Version` header. Thoughts? Design doc: https://redwood.infer/notes/response-metadata :eyes:

kyle: 6 weeks seems tight for some enterprise customers. I'd push to 8 weeks, or at least make the default server behavior remain v1 unless client explicitly asks for v2. Also wondering about SDKs: do we want them to opt-in automatically? :thinking_face:

mara: agree we should keep v1 default. SDKs should NOT auto opt-in on minor releases. Suggestion: SDKs expose a `responseVersion` param and default to 1. We'll document how to opt-in.

sylvia: how does this interact with streaming? If we add `metadata` to the envelope, do we emit it mid-stream or only at the final event?

mara: streaming plan is to keep token stream identical, and emit metadata as a final SSE event (or final chunk) so existing streaming consumers are unaffected. Example SSE snippet:
```
event: metadata
data: {"request_id":"abc123","model_version":"v2","prompt_hash":"sha256:..."}
```
This keeps tokens as-is and appends metadata after stream end.

aj: SDK work: JS + Python need a small shim. Steps I see: add opt-in flag, add parser for final metadata event, add tests. Also add a compatibility integration test in CI that verifies v1 clients still get the old envelope. No auto-upgrade.

kyle: monitoring/telemetry: add a `response_contract_version` metric (labels: client_sdk, region, model) and an alert if >1% of production traffic is seeing 4xx/5xx after we flip any routing. Also add an eval job to our regression suite to ensure nll/perplexity doesn't regress for top-10 prompts.

devops-bot: Staging rollout started: service=responses, config=response-metadata-dual-shipping=true, rollout=10% -> 50% -> 100% (manual gates). Logs: https://ci.redwood/infer/builds/4421 :rocket:

mara: Comms plan draft: (1) announce in #announcements 2 weeks before window start, (2) email top-50 accounts with migration guide, (3) add console banner with opt-in toggle, (4) publish SDK upgrade guides and a migration snippet.

kyle: small API detail question — header name? `Accept-Response-Version` vs `X-RW-Response-Version`? I prefer the standard-y `Accept-Response-Version` so proxies/caches behave normally.

sylvia: also add a `X-RW-Contract-Token` response header containing the server-side contract hash so we can trace mismatches in logs.

mara: agreed on `Accept-Response-Version` as the opt-in header, and we'll add `X-RW-Contract-Hash` in responses. Example request/response:
```
GET /v1/responses
Accept-Response-Version: 2

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RW-Contract-Hash: sha256:deadbeef
{ "id": "r1", "text":"...", "metadata": { "model_version":"v2", "request_id":"..." } }
```

aj: I'll add SDK PRs targeting the opt-in flag this week. Can someone own the customer email?

kyle: I'll take the customer email + top-50 list. Can we get a plain-language migration snippet for README? Keep it 3 lines.

mara: Action items: 
- @aj create SDK PRs (js/py) and CI tests (due EOW)
- @kyle draft customer comms + migration snippet (due Tue)
- @sylvia add telemetry + regression eval (due Thu)
- @mara prepare console banner + docs (due next Wed)

mara: If no objections I'll start the 6-week dual-ship window proposal in the design doc and ping legal/enterprise for the timeline. :thumbsup:

kyle: +1 from me. Let's make the window start 2 weeks after we ship the console banner and SDK PRs merge.

sylvia: +1

aj: +1, will open PRs today.

mara: OK locking this in. Will post a follow-up with exact dates and a tiny migration snippet once SDK PRs are open. Thanks everyone! :tada:
